title: Splat Studio
tagline: Turn a phone video or photos into an explorable 3D scene, trained live on your own graphics card.
description:
A complete 3D Gaussian Splatting trainer and viewer that runs in the browser tab with WebGPU. Try the pre-trained vintage camera (30.8 dB on photos the trainer never saw) or a real scanned teddy bear (36.7 dB, soft fur), then watch a scene learn from scratch, or add your own photos or a video. The page works out where each photo was taken (its own structure-from-motion), picks sharp video frames, down-weights blurry ones, evens out brightness differences between photos, can cut one object out of a cluttered background or keep a whole room, and trains in 200, 400 or 800 pixel quality. Everything runs locally; nothing is uploaded.

Reproduced from the paper: the local-PCA surface regulariser (eigenvalue loss and normal alignment). Added around it: tile-based WebGPU rasteriser with analytic gradients, SSIM loss, view-dependent colour (SH degree 1), importance pruning, joint camera refinement, Blur-Trap style random splitting, compact demo files, and a from-scratch camera solver.

Not reproduced: the paper's DTU / Tanks and Temples / mesh and Poisson experiments, learned pruning masks, and higher SH degrees. Camera solving is a compact home-made solver, not COLMAP; it needs smooth, overlapping, textured captures. Object cut-out is automatic and imperfect.

Demo assets: Camera 01 by Rajil Jose Macatangay via Poly Haven (CC0); teddy bear from Google Research Scanned Objects (CC BY 4.0, Google LLC 2020).
novelty: No known in-browser WebGPU implementation of PCAsplat combined with on-device camera solving (not verified).
howItWorks: Blobs (3D Gaussians) are drawn from each photo's camera, compared with the real photo, and nudged by analytic gradients computed in WGSL shaders. PCAsplat looks at each blob's 16 nearest neighbours and pulls blobs onto thin surfaces. For your own media, Harris/BRIEF features, RANSAC and bundle adjustment solve the cameras first.
controls: Drag to orbit, right-drag or two fingers to pan, scroll or pinch to zoom. Press F (or Walk around) for first-person mode: click to capture the mouse, W A S D to walk, Shift to run, Q / E down and up, scroll for speed, Esc to release. Pick a demo or switch to Use my own.

paper.title: PCAsplat: Gaussian Splatting with Local PCA Regularization
